intro: Lesson 7: Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb: buildings as sources. To understand the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb and how buildings can be used as historical sources

model.title: What does the Taj Mahal tell us?

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Who: Shah Jahan, as a tomb

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Shows: huge wealth, skilled workers, Persian and Indian styles

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Shows: Qur'anic calligraphy, so Islam mattered

parts.label: Step 4
parts.text: Leaves out: the lives of ordinary workers and farmers

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: A rich, skilled, Muslim court; little about ordinary people.

questions.q: What does the Red Fort tell us about Shah Jahan's empire?
questions.a: It was rich, powerful and had skilled builders
questions.model: Ask the source questions. Who: Shah Jahan. What it shows: a huge, strong, beautiful fort. So the empire was rich and powerful.

questions.q: Why did Shah Jahan's sons fight?
questions.a: There was no fixed rule of succession, so each wanted the throne

questions.q: Give one reason historians disagree about Aurangzeb.
questions.a: They focus on different evidence: his piety and conquests, or his wars and treatment of rivals

questions.q: Core: Source task: for the Taj Mahal and the Badshahi Mosque, write who built it, what it shows, and what it does not show.
questions.a: Taj Mahal: Shah Jahan; wealth, skill, Islamic faith; not ordinary lives. Badshahi Mosque: Aurangzeb; faith and power; not the cost of wars
questions.model: Teacher does the Taj Mahal row first, using the model slide.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain why interpretations of Aurangzeb differ.
questions.a: Historians use different sources and ask different questions; some focus on piety and expansion, others on wars and conflict

questions.q: Stretch: Are buildings more or less reliable than written sources? Explain.
questions.a: They are real and hard to fake, but show rulers' views and leave out ordinary people

questions.q: Big question: what can the Taj Mahal tell us that a book cannot?
questions.a: Physical evidence of wealth, skill, style and faith, seen directly rather than through a writer's view
